newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on long liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Thursday due to long liquidation, with most investors not wanting to deliver physical goods, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended limit-down at 3,162 yuan ($381) per tonne, losing 94 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 3,300.
January rose four yuan to 3,165, March fell eight to 3,190, May dropped 20 to 3,280, July rose 60 to 3,370 and September rose on 60 to 3,380.
Combined volume rose to 24,300 tonnes from 1,460.
Traders said most investors did not want to deliver physical goods with the approach of the delivery day of the November contract next Tuesday.

"Many investors liquidated their long positions in the November contract due to over-supply of spot soybean," one trader said. "Despite rebounds of some contracts today, the future trend is not bright due to poor fundamentals."
Analysts expect soybean to continue falling in the next few days.
